t:
Section 204(l)(2) of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1154(l)(2)) is amended—
    (1) in subparagraph (E), by striking “or” at the end; 
    (2) by redesignating subparagraph (F) as subparagraph (G); and 
    (3) by inserting after subparagraph (E) the following:“(F) a child of an alien who filed a pending or approved petition for classification or application for adjustment of status or other benefit specified in section 101(a)(51) as a VAWA self-petitioner; or”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the word "petition" signals an outside party formally engaging the government. Here it refers to an immigration petition or application for a benefit by a VAWA self-petitioner, and applications for benefits are expressly excluded from participation. The section only adds a category of eligible aliens to an existing provision and creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
fable.s: a child of an alien who filed a pending or approved petition for classification or application for adjustment of status or other benefit

opus.w: This amendment only adds children of VAWA self-petitioners to a list of covered people in an immigration statute. The "petition" and "application" it mentions are individual requests for immigration benefits, and the definition excludes applications for benefits. Nothing here creates a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or a right to sue over a federal decision.
opus.s: a child of an alien who filed a pending or approved petition for classification or application for adjustment of status or other benefit specified in section 101(a)(51) as a VAWA self-petitioner

qwen_chat.w: This section amends eligibility criteria for immigration benefits. It references petitions and applications for status, which the definition explicitly excludes as 'applications for benefits or grants.' There is no requirement for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees involved in the decision-making process described here.
qwen_chat.s: (F) a child of an alien who filed a pending or approved petition for classification or application for adjustment of status or other benefit specified in section 101(a)(51) as a VAWA self-petitioner; or
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions a "petition" or "application," it involves participation. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits or grants" are not participation. Furthermore, this section is merely amending the eligibility criteria for immigration status (specifically regarding children of VAWA self-petitioners); it does not establish a process for public comment, consultation, or advisory input into a federal decision. The "petition" mentioned is an application for a benefit, which is excluded.
